encodes the direction and distance to a food source (or nest site) in a figure-eight movement on the vertical comb, and nestmates use that information to fly directly to the target. it is the only known non-human signal that encodes two continuous spatial variables simultaneously. what the signal is the dance is a figure-eight performed on vertical comb in the dark hive: waggle phase: the bee runs in a straight line while vibrating its abdomen side-to-side. this is the information-bearing segment. return phase: the bee circles back to the start — alternating right and left turns between successive waggle runs. the dance is multimodal. the waggle bee simultaneously: performs the visual movement releases alkanes and alkenes onto its abdomen and into the air (chemical) produces wing vibrations (acoustic) emits electric fields detectable by nestmates' johnston's organs in their antennae (electric — a recently discovered channel) what it encodes direction: the angle of the waggle run relative to vertical = the angle of the food source relative to the sun. if the waggle run points straight up, the food is directly toward the sun. bees automatically adjust this angle as the sun moves across the sky — a dance performed an hour after scouting still gives accurate directions. distance: the duration of the waggle run. longer waggle run = farther food source. round dances (no waggle) communicate nearby resources (<10m); transitional dances for 20–30m; full waggle dance for >40m. quality: the urgency and repetition rate of the dance. more excited waggling = higher-quality resource. competing bees actively disrupt each other's dances or fight — the dance is a competition to recruit nestmates. danger: foragers that encountered a dead bee on a flower perform fewer dances — encoding risk into the recruitment signal (abbott & dukas, 2009). karl von frisch called the encoded information *tanzsprache* ("dance language"). he received the nobel prize in 1973 for its does it actually work? the most surprising finding about the waggle dance is how rarely receivers use it. studies show: 93% of foragers who thoroughly followed a waggle dance returned to foraging areas they already knew only ~10% of foragers actually use the dance's location information receivers use the dance as a *trigger* for foraging activity, not as a navigation instruction. they then use private memory, odor cues from the dancer, or random search. the dance location information is primarily useful when private information is depleted — in tropical environments with sparse, patchy flowering trees, colonies without waggle dancing fail at foraging. in temperate environments with homogeneous patches, colonies can forage successfully even when dance information is experimentally obscured. this changes the interpretation: the waggle dance is not a command-and-control broadcast to naive foragers, but a social tipping mechanism that reactivates experienced foragers when the colony's collective memory needs updating. dialects different *apis* species and subspecies have different "dialects" — the mapping between waggle run duration and distance varies by species. in a search: jakob von uexküll and the umwelt concept jakob-von-uexkull-umwelt umwelt theory umwelt concept von uexküll biosemiotics founding subjective perceptual world jakob von uexküll and the umwelt concept jakob johann von uexküll (1864–1944) was a baltic german biologist who proposed the *umwelt* — the species-specific subjective perceptual world each organism inhabits. it is the f… jakob von uexküll and the umwelt concept jakob johann von uexküll (1864–1944) was a baltic german biologist who proposed the *umwelt* — the species-specific subjective perceptual world each organism inhabits. it is the founding concept of biosemiotics and the conceptual anchor for this vault. the core idea every organism lives within a bounded perceptual world constituted entirely by the signs its sense organs can receive and the actions its effectors can produce. this is the *umwelt*. it is not the physical environment — that uexküll called the *umgebung* — but the organism's own subset of reality, the only reality it can act within. the mechanism is a closed feedback loop: sensors (*merkorgan*) detect the state of the umwelt → a central processing stage connects perception to action → effectors (*werkorgan*) change the umwelt → new sensor input. uexküll called this the "function-circle." what we now call sensorimotor coupling. the tick example uexküll's most famous illustration: the blind, deaf tick (*ixodes*) waiting on a blade of grass. its entire umwelt is reduced to three signals: butyric acid odor — released by mammalian sebaceous glands; causes the tick to drop 37°c warmth — warmth of mammalian blood; causes the tick to seek skin hairlessness — tactile search for thin skin; causes the tick to burrow and feed a creature with only three functional signs. the entire richness of a forest — light, wind, other organisms, time — does not exist for it. uexküll documented ticks that had waited 18 years without food in laboratory conditions, perfectly inert until a butyric acid signal arrived. the tick example is the paradigm case for this vault: the umwelt is not a simplified map of the environment, it *is* the environment, from that organism's perspective. umwelt vs. umgebung umwelt — the world as the organism constitutes it through its senses and actions; the only world that organism can perceive or affect umgebung — the physical surroundings as observed from *outside* (typically the human observer's perspective) innenwelt — the proximal, unmediated sensory data; the organism's immediate inner experience before interpretation the umgebung/innenwelt relationship must be learned in infancy — this anticipates embodied cognition. why this vault is named umwelt this vault maps the *signals that cross between umwelten*. when a vervet monkey produces a "eagle" call, it is emitting a sign that exists in *its* umwelt and is received by conspecifics whose umwelten contain the corresponding sign-receptor. when a diana monkey's alarm call is understood by a hornbill, a sign bridges two radically different umwelten. the study of animal communication is the study of how incompatible subjective worlds can nonetheless make contact. legacy and influence uexküll established biosemiotics as a field. his work directly influenced: heidegger — the concept of *dasein* and being-in-the-world merleau-ponty — embodied perception deleuze and guattari — *a thousand plateaus* uses umwelt extensively thomas sebeok — built zoosemiotics on uexküll's foundation ed yong — *an immense world* (2022) is essentially a popular account of umwelten key work: *a foray into the worlds of animals and humans* (1934); english translation by joseph d. o'neil, university of minnesota press (2010). open questions whether the umwelt framework can accommodate social cognition — the vervet alarm call problem suggests that some organisms' umwelten contain representations *of other organisms' umwelten* the relationship between umwelt and consciousness: uexküll treats all organisms as subjects, but on what basis? his complicated national socialist entanglement (1933 hitler pledge, 2021 scholarship by schnödl & sprenger revealing deep involvement) — his framework's subsequent use by theorists of difference and becoming is ironic given his political commitments
